title: Safe Execution: Timeouts to Audit
objective: After this lesson you will be able to bound tool execution (timeouts, retries with backoff), make money tools idempotent, return isError results instead of throwing, and keep stdout protocol-clean with audit flowing elsewhere.
why: Exposed tools meet production reality: slow upstreams, duplicate deliveries, crashing handlers, noisy logs. Each failure mode has a structural answer — timeouts with budgets, idempotency keys with check-before-act, isError envelopes, stderr logging. Safe execution is what separates demo servers from deployed ones; this lesson is the deployment checklist as engineering.

blocks.text: Every tool call gets a **timeout** (slow upstreams must not hang runs) and **bounded retries with backoff** (transients deserve chances, persistents deserve escalation). Timeouts compose: tool timeout < caller timeout < run budget — nested limits with headroom at each level. Retry budgets count attempts AND time; attempts-only budgets hang on slow failures.

blocks.caption: Timeouts race, retries backoff, failures return — never throw, never hang

blocks.text: Idempotency: money tools run twice safely

Retries, replays, and crash recovery re-invoke tools — **idempotency keys** (caller-supplied per logical operation) plus **check-before-act** (key seen? return recorded outcome) make repeats safe. Refunds, charges, and sends all key by operation ID; lookups stay naturally idempotent. Unkeyed money tools double-apply on recovery — the incident class idempotency exists to delete.

blocks.caption: Keys + check-before-act: repeats return records, never re-execute

blocks.text: Handler failures return `{content: [...readable...], isError: true}` — the model reads, reacts (clarify, retry fixed, escalate), and the run continues debuggably. Raw throws break runs opaquely mid-protocol. And **stdout carries JSON-RPC**: log to stderr (or OpenTelemetry); one stray console.log on stdout corrupts framing for every subsequent message. Transport hygiene is a deployment gate, not a suggestion.

blocks.title: Prove idempotency
blocks.note: Run it: expect charges=1 after the repeat (replay, not re-execution), r2 flagged replay, then a fresh key executing (charges=2). Crash-recovery duplicates become free — keys convert replays into records.

items: Timeouts race, retries backoff with attempt+time budgets; failures return as data
Idempotency keys + check-before-act (+durable key store in production) make repeats safe
isError envelopes keep failures routable; stdout stays protocol-clean (stderr/OpenTelemetry for logs)

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice idempotency proof and confirm charges=1 across the repeat. (b) Extend with a failing first attempt (throw once, then succeed) wrapped in boundedCall: prove retry-then-success with attempts counted. (c) State where the memory-map keys must move for production durability, and what breaks if they don't.
hints: Baseline: charges=1, r2 replay=true, r3 fresh with charges=2 — repeats are records.
Fail-once fn + boundedCall(tries 2): first throws, backoff, second succeeds — attempts counted, failure never thrown outward.
Production: keys in durable store (DB unique constraint on operation key); memory maps die with crashes — the exact window idempotency must cover.
exercise.why: Repeat-safety (keys), transient-tolerance (bounded retries), and durability (surviving crashes) are the three execution guarantees — each verified, with the production gap (memory vs durable keys) stated honestly.

quiz.q: Refund tool retried after a crash double-charges. Missing?
options: Idempotency keys + check-before-act in a durable store — repeats return records
quiz.explain: Recovery re-invokes: unkeyed money tools double-apply. Keys make repeats safe; durability (DB unique) covers crashes.

quiz.q: console.log debugging inside a stdio MCP server. Risk?
options: stdout corruption: protocol framing breaks on non-JSON-RPC bytes — log to stderr/OpenTelemetry
quiz.explain: stdout IS the wire for stdio transport. One stray log corrupts every subsequent message's framing.

quiz.q: Tool hangs on slow upstream with no timeout. Fix shape?
options: Race with timeout + bounded backoff retries; failures return as data — nested limits with headroom per level
quiz.explain: Unbounded waits hang runs opaquely. Timeouts race, retries backoff, budgets bound attempts AND time.

summary: Bounded calls, idempotent money, isError envelopes, clean stdout. Safe execution is deployment checklist as code.
